muc.title: Praised in practice, frozen for real
muc.text: You practice interviews with AI ten times, and get praised every time. At the real interview, the interviewer is cold and fires questions at you, and you freeze.

muc.title: AI is too easygoing
muc.text: Trap one: AI role-play is usually too easygoing. It's trained to be polite, so even a "difficult" customer is much softer than in real life.

muc.title: Real life has more
muc.text: Trap two: a simulation is just a simple version of real life. It leaves out a lot, like a shaky voice, noise and time pressure.

muc.title: AI can make things up
muc.text: Trap three: AI can make things up. The numbers in a budget simulation, or the procedure in a branching scenario, may not match reality.

muc.title: Review after every practice
muc.text: The fix: ask for real difficulty, and always do a debrief, a review after practice: where did I go wrong, and what will I do differently next time?

muc.title: Simulation is a stepping stone
muc.text: And before the real thing, practice with a real person too. Simulations help you prepare, but they can't replace the real thing.

muc.title: The whole series in one picture
muc.text: The whole series: practice without fear of mistakes, virtual labs, role-play, branching scenarios, homemade simulations, and how to avoid the traps.

muc.title: Grade me strictly
muc.text: After each practice with AI, ask it: grade me as strictly as a real person would, and point out my three biggest mistakes. Next series: interactive learning with AI.
